newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE president says U.S. biased towards Israel.
newsitem.headline: UAE president says U.S. biased towards Israel.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates considered the United States biased towards Israel in the Middle East peace process and urged Washington to be fair, UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan said in remarks published on Friday.
"Always taking from one party does not work," Sheikh Zaid said in an interview in London with the Arabic daily Al-Hayat.

The London-based newspaper said: "Sheikh Zaid...welcomed a resumption of mediation by the United States between the Palestinians and Israel. "But he does not expect a positive outcome of the mediation, saying the Americans were biased towards Israel."
U.S. mediator Dennis Ross will travel to the region this weekend in an attempt to calm tensions after two suicide bombers killed 13 people in a Jerusalem market on July 30.
Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Wednesday she also planned to visit the Middle East for the first time later this month.

Sheikh Zaid, who marked the 31st anniversary of his accession to power on Wednesday, said his government had formed its opinion about U.S. mediation after talks with Defence Secretary William Cohen during a visit to the UAE in June.
The president said his government's contacts with the United States continued.

Sheikh Zaid, who is on a private visit to Britain, was due to travel to the United States on Sunday for medical tests, the daily said. He had surgery on a vertebra in his neck at the Mayo Clinic in Minnesota last September. The president is 78.
